items.followUp: State Newton’s second law of motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Newton’s first law describes how a body’s state of rest or uniform straight-line motion changes only when an unbalanced external force acts on it.
rubric.description: States Newton’s first law of motion.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a statement covering rest or uniform straight-line motion and the role of an external unbalanced force; award 1 mark if substantially correct but incomplete.

rubric.why: A passenger tends to continue moving when a bus stops suddenly, illustrating inertia of motion.
rubric.description: Gives one suitable example of Newton’s first law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly described example, such as a passenger moving forward when a bus stops suddenly.

rubric.why: Dust tends to remain at rest as the carpet moves, illustrating inertia.
rubric.description: Gives a second, distinct suitable example of Newton’s first law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly described second example, such as dust falling from a beaten carpet.

modelAnswer: Newton’s first law states that a body remains at rest or continues to move with uniform speed in a straight line unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.
When a moving bus stops suddenly, a passenger tends to move forward because the body tends to continue in motion.
When a carpet is beaten, dust particles fall off because they tend to remain at rest while the carpet moves.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and derive its equation.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with a body’s position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating potential energy to position or configuration.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows energy associated with position.
rubric.description: Gives an example of potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as a raised body or water stored in a dam.

rubric.why: The derivation identifies the lifting force as the body’s weight, mg, and the distance moved as height h.
rubric.description: Sets up the work done in raising the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the force as mg and the distance as h.

rubric.why: Work done against gravity is stored as gravitational potential energy, giving PE = mgh.
rubric.description: Obtains the equation for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving or stating PE = mgh.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body because of its position or configuration.
For example, a raised body has gravitational potential energy.
To raise a body of mass m through a height h, the force applied against gravity is equal to its weight: F = mg.
Work done = force × distance = mg × h = mgh.
This work is stored as potential energy; therefore, PE = mgh.

items.followUp: State Pascal’s law and explain how it is used in a hydraulic machine.

rubric.why: Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted undiminished throughout the liquid and in every direction.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the complete principle; award 1 mark if pressure transmission is stated but the principle is incomplete.

rubric.why: The hydraulic press works because the pressure on its two pistons is equal: F1/A1 = F2/A2.
rubric.description: Applies Pascal’s law to the two pistons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct pressure relation or its verbal equivalent.

rubric.why: The larger-area piston produces a greater force and can lift a heavy load.
rubric.description: Explains how a hydraulic press multiplies force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a larger piston can exert a larger force or lift a heavy load.

modelAnswer: Pascal’s law states that pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions throughout the liquid.
A hydraulic press has two pistons of different areas connected by an enclosed liquid.
By Pascal’s law, the pressures at the two pistons are equal: P1 = P2, so F1/A1 = F2/A2.
Since the area of the larger piston is greater, it exerts a larger force and can lift a heavy load.

rubric.why: Scientific notation writes a number as a coefficient multiplied by a power of ten, with the coefficient at least 1 and less than 10.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a number is written as a product involving a power of ten and an appropriate coefficient.

rubric.why: The example 300,000,000 = 3 × 10⁸ correctly demonstrates scientific notation.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example in scientific notation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as 300,000,000 = 3 × 10⁸.

modelAnswer: Scientific notation expresses a number as a product of a number from 1 up to but not including 10 and a power of 10.
